The table data elements were not interacting well with inline styles (in the rich sense) and the table data element would have its content overridden every time we found another excerpt of text with a different style.

steps.message: I have fixed the issue where markdown table data elements were overriding their content instead of appending it when encountering inline styles. I also fixed a typo in the `create` method of `TableDataElement`. I verified the fix with a test script.

The issue was that `TableDataElement.on_text` in `rich/markdown.py` was replacing `self.content` with a new `Text` object every time it was called, instead of appending the new text to the existing content. This caused content to be lost when inline styles or links were present in table cells.

I fixed this by:
1. Initializing `self.content` as a `Text` object in `TableDataElement.__init__`.
2. Updating `TableDataElement.on_text` to use the `append` method of the `Text` object, similar to how `TextElement.on_text` is implemented.
3. Also fixed a typo in `TableDataElement.create` where `token.attrs.get("style" "")` was used instead of `token.attrs.get("style", "")`.

These changes ensure that all text within a table cell is preserved and correctly styled.
